timingsRecaptureMethod: HISTORICAL (superseded by timingsRecaptureMethodUpdate below; kept for how the 2026-08-05 generation under supersededSampleRuns was produced). toon#151. `gateSpeed` and `gatePerformance.runnerMinutes` were re-measured against the workflow's CURRENT job set, via `gh api repos/toon-protocol/toon/actions/runs/<id>/attempts/1/jobs` for the 5 most recent `push`-to-`main` runs of ci.yml as of 2026-08-05 (run ids in `sampleRuns`; the same 5-most-recent-push-runs rule as the original capture). Only the two GATED jobs are counted — `build` and `Devbox Environment Validation`. The `Gate speed/performance no-regression guard` job itself is excluded: it observes the run, it is not part of the work being measured, and it is always still in progress when it reads the API. Note that `Build sandcastle agent image` belongs to a DIFFERENT workflow (agent-image.yml) with its own run id, so it has never appeared in this run's job list and does not affect these figures — its size is gated separately by `dockerImageSize`. The recaptured summed runner-seconds (154.6) came out identical to the 2026-07-22 capture, i.e. the gate's compute has not drifted; only the wall-clock figure needed replacing, and it was replaced by a queue-immune metric rather than re-averaged.
timingsRecaptureMethodUpdate: toon#173. The 2026-08-05 capture above sampled only `push`-to-`main` runs, but `gate-regression-guard` gates every `pull_request` run too (ci.yml:112, `needs: [build, devbox-validate]`, both of which run `if: github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'pull_request'`) -- so that sample undercounted real variance. Proof: the PR run that actually gated #157 (run 31187288497, head 7b125eb, merged as 430a358) measured a 120.0s longest job / 164.0s summed runner-seconds, both above every 2026-08-05 sampleRun, yet was never eligible for inclusion under the push-only rule. Re-recaptured 2026-08-07 from the 5 most recent COMPLETED ci.yml runs of EITHER event type (`gh run list --workflow=ci.yml --json databaseId,headSha,createdAt,event,conclusion --limit 15`, most recent first, skipping non-`success` runs), via the same per-run `gh api .../attempts/1/jobs` read as before. See `sampleRuns[].event` for which of the 5 were `push` vs `pull_request`.

gateShape.test: vitest run (via `pnpm -r test --if-present` in CI, plus `npx vitest run .sandcastle/` for the root-config guard + parity tests)

method: Representative sample = the 5 most recent `push`-to-`main` runs of .github/workflows/ci.yml as of capturedAt, read via `gh run list --workflow=ci.yml --json ...` / `gh run view <id> --json jobs` / `gh api repos/toon-protocol/toon/actions/runs/<id>/timing`. Correctness counts taken directly from a clean checkout of capturedFromCommit via `npx eslint . -f json` and `pnpm run typecheck`, not from CI logs (CI truncates neither, but a local run is simpler to reproduce byte-for-byte). See `sampleRuns` for the raw per-run figures this baseline was averaged from. HISTORICAL NOTE for reproduction: at capturedFromCommit the root `vitest run` script spuriously failed ~50 sdk tests that passed under CI's per-package command, because the root vitest.config.ts omitted the `TOON_GENESIS_PEERS: '[]'` hermetic-fixture env that packages/sdk/vitest.config.ts sets (toon#79). That is FIXED: toon#146 added the env to the root config (50 failed -> 0 failed / 2308 passed / 6 skipped) and toon#144 added `.sandcastle/vitest-config-parity.test.ts`, run by the blocking `Gate guard unit tests (incl. root vitest config parity)` step, which fails the build if a package config ever again sets a `test.env` var the root config does not apply. Either command now reproduces a clean run; `pnpm -r test --if-present` remains the one whose timings this baseline measured.

gateSpeed.description: Execution time of the ci.yml workflow's gated jobs (`build` and `Devbox Environment Validation`; the `Gate speed/performance no-regression guard` job is excluded because it measures the run rather than being part of it). The GATED figure is `averageLongestJobDurationSeconds`: the measured jobs run in parallel, so on a free runner pool the longest of them IS the run's wall-clock, and unlike the raw span it cannot be inflated by runner queue depth.
gateSpeed.averageTotalRunDurationSecondsNote: INFORMATIONAL, NOT GATED (toon#151). max(job completed_at) - min(job started_at). All five recaptured runs were scheduled onto free runners (6.4s average total queue), so the span happens to equal the longest job here — that coincidence is exactly why the previous 112s span baseline looked sound and then false-FAILed the moment the org's runner pool was saturated (toon#150 measured a 402.0s span for 147.0s of compute). The guard prints this number for context and never compares against it.
gateSpeed.regressionToleranceRationale: toon#153, corrected by toon#173. The 50% band inherited from the retired span metric (toon#151) was sized for a queue-inflated quantity that could swing tens of seconds run-to-run; averageLongestJobDurationSeconds is a job duration and is far steadier. toon#173 re-recaptured sampleRuns to include pull_request-gated runs (see timingsRecaptureMethodUpdate) after discovering the #153 rationale's push-only sample had missed the run that actually gated #157. Over the current 5 sampleRuns, longestJobSeconds (104, 120, 115, 115, 116) deviate at most 8.8% from the new 114.0s mean (observedMaxDeviationFraction; the 104s low outlier). 20% is roughly 2.3x that observed spread -- tighter than the 3x toon#153 claimed, but still enough that no sampleRun would false-FAIL -- while still catching a genuine 40% compute regression (114.0s -> 159.6s exceeds the 136.8s allowance). Real headroom above the top observed sample (120s) is ~14.0%, under the ~15% comfort margin toon#173 asked to flag rather than silently tolerate.

gatePerformance.description: Runner cost & cache efficiency. `toon` is a PUBLIC repo, so GitHub bills $0 regardless of minutes used (billable minutes always report 0 via the Actions API) — raw job-second totals are recorded instead as the cost proxy.

runnerMinutes.unit: raw job-seconds summed across both gated ci.yml jobs (build + Devbox Environment Validation), NOT GitHub-billed minutes
runnerMinutes.recapturedNote: toon#151 re-measured this against the current job set on 2026-08-05 and got 154.6 again (per-run: 158, 149, 153, 156, 157), unchanged from the 2026-07-22 capture. toon#173 then re-recaptured on 2026-08-07 with a push+pull_request sample (see timingsRecaptureMethodUpdate) and got 163.2 (per-run: 158, 164, 159, 167, 168) -- summed job-seconds is still execution time only and never includes queue time, which is why this metric passed throughout the toon#150 incident while the span-based speed metric failed; the increase from 154.6 to 163.2 reflects the broadened, more representative sample, not a regression.
runnerMinutes.regressionToleranceRationale: toon#153, corrected by toon#173. Over the current 5 sampleRuns, sumRunnerSeconds (158, 164, 159, 167, 168) deviate at most 3.2% from the new 163.2s mean (observedMaxDeviationFraction; the 158s low outlier) -- still tighter than gateSpeed's spread, so this figure keeps the tighter band. 15% is roughly 4.7x that observed spread, comfortably clearing the top observed sample (168s, +2.9%), while still catching a genuine 40% compute regression (163.2s -> 228.5s exceeds the 187.7s allowance). Real headroom above the top observed sample (168s) is ~11.7%, under the ~15% comfort margin -- flagged per toon#173 rather than silently widened.
runnerMinutes.billedMinutesNote: Public repo — GitHub-hosted Actions minutes are free; the Actions API always reports billable.UBUNTU.total_ms=0 for this repo regardless of actual runner time.

cacheHitRate.pnpmDependencyCache: 4/5 (80%) — action: actions/setup-node@v7 with cache: pnpm. The one miss was the run whose pnpm-lock.yaml changed, which correctly invalidates the cache key.
cacheHitRate.devboxCliAndNixStoreCache: 5/5 (100%) — action: jetify-com/devbox-install-action in the Devbox Environment Validation job.

dockerImageSize.note: The .sandcastle/Dockerfile agent image (sandcastle:toon) has no prior run that recorded its size — .github/workflows/agent-image.yml only ever asserted the image builds and its toolchain is correct. This change adds a 'Report agent image size' step (docker image inspect --format '{{.Size}}') to that workflow so the number is captured on its next run. This capture environment has neither a Docker daemon nor push access to trigger that workflow, so the figure could not be filled in here — update this field from that step's log output once available, without re-deriving the rest of the baseline.

gateCorrectness.description: Current violation counts under the existing soft-gate ceiling (`eslint . --max-warnings 940`) and the known-debt typecheck gate. These are the frozen baseline the epic (toon-protocol/toon-meta#210) ratchets toward zero in follow-up slices — this issue only captures the number.

typecheck.note: HISTORICAL. 246 was the soft-gate debt captured at capturedFromCommit, when typecheck was not wired into ci.yml as a blocking step (toon#110, the toon Part-of-#111 commit message). That debt is now fully paid: #126/#128/#131/#132/#134/#136/#139/#140/#142 ratcheted 246 -> 1, and toon#144 removed the last error and added a blocking `Typecheck` step to the ci.yml `build` job. The live ceiling is now 0 errors, enforced by `tsc --noEmit`'s own exit code rather than by a number in this file -- there is no typecheck guard subcommand in gate-guard-cli.ts because zero needs no threshold.

sampleRuns.note: toon#173: the PR run that actually gated #157; excluded from the toon#151 push-only sample despite being subject to the same gate (ci.yml:112).

supersededSampleRuns.note: Prior captures' raw per-run figures, kept for history, oldest first. The 2026-07-22 generation's `totalRunDurationSeconds` is the span metric toon#151 retired. The 2026-08-05 generation is the push-only job-duration sample toon#173 superseded after finding it missed the pull_request-gated runs the guard also enforces (see the live `sampleRuns` above and `timingsRecaptureMethodUpdate`).
